newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees tax on "callback" phone services.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees tax on "callback" phone services.

text.p: The European Union adopted rules Monday to allow national governments to tax telephone services offered by foreign companies, a move aimed especially at "callback" services operating in the United States.

The legislation agreed by EU economic and finance ministers would also allow governments to exempt from taxes telecom services offered by EU companies to customers abroad -- a move the European Commission said was inappropriate.

The initiative was prompted by the growing popularity of services that allow consumers to bypass high European phone charges by dialing a U.S. number and getting called back with an open phone line to make calls at low U.S. rates.
Those calls are not now subject to national value-added taxes, which range from 15 percent to 25 percent in the EU.

The Commission, responding to a unaminous request from EU governments, proposed that foreign firms be required to charge value-added tax on telecoms services offered to EU customers -- putting them on a par with their European counterparts.
